projectState.overview: StreamTube is a YouTube-like video sharing platform built as an MBA greenfield challenge. Monorepo with a NestJS 11 backend (nestjs-project/) and a Next.js 16 frontend (next-frontend/). Phases 01 (base config), 02 (auth — backend + frontend) and 03 (video upload and processing) are fully implemented, tested and merged into main. Phase 03 delivered all 9 Small Increments: Docker Compose infra (Redis + MinIO), the Video entity and migration, the full S3 multipart upload lifecycle (initiate, presign-part, abort, complete), the BullMQ video-processing queue, a dedicated FFmpeg worker container, video streaming/download via presigned-GET redirects, and the public video-info endpoint.
projectState.overviewWorkingTree: The working tree is currently on branch fix/startup-infra with staged-but-uncommitted planning artifacts for a new task, task-startup-infra: a Docker startup/infra reliability fix for the Phase 03 stack so a clean `docker compose up -d --build` is operational on any host. Its research, technical decisions, consolidated context and validation (status: clean) are written; implementation of the fix has NOT started yet.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 01 — Base Configuration
implementedFeatures.summary: Full project foundation: monorepo structure, NestJS 11 initialized, Docker Compose with PostgreSQL + Mailpit, TypeORM with DataSource and migration runner, environment validation via Joi, namespaced config with registerAs, Swagger/OpenAPI export, ESLint + Prettier.
implementedFeatures.notes: All services use Docker Compose service names as hosts (never localhost). Migrations run via npm run migration:run. Config organized per domain in src/config/ using registerAs factories.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Backend (NestJS)
implementedFeatures.summary: Full authentication system: user registration with email confirmation, login with JWT access+refresh tokens, logout, forgot/reset password flow, channel auto-creation from email prefix. All flows tested with unit + integration + E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: JWT stored in HttpOnly cookies. Refresh token rotation implemented. Channel nickname derived from email prefix. ChannelsService owns channel creation; UsersService compensates by deleting user if channel creation fails. Public decorator skips JWT guard. DomainException with custom filter.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 02 — Auth Frontend (Next.js)
implementedFeatures.summary: Auth screens built with Next.js App Router: signup, login, forgot-password. BFF API routes proxy to NestJS backend. Session managed via iron-session HttpOnly cookies. RHF + Zod validation. MSW mocks for all auth routes in test. Playwright E2E tests.
implementedFeatures.notes: OpenAPI types generated into lib/api/types.gen.ts. MSW enabled via MSW_ENABLED=true env var at server startup. Design system: Tailwind CSS 4, custom UI primitives in components/ui/. Playwright for E2E tests, Vitest for unit tests.

implementedFeatures.name: Phase 03 — Video Upload & Processing (complete, merged to main)
implementedFeatures.summary: End-to-end video pipeline across all 9 SIs: S3 multipart upload for files up to 10GB (initiate, presign-part, complete, abort), BullMQ video-processing queue, a dedicated FFmpeg worker container that extracts metadata (ffprobe) and generates a thumbnail (ffmpeg) then marks the video READY/FAILED, presigned-GET 302 redirects for streaming and download, and a public video-info endpoint. All SIs tested (unit + integration + E2E).
implementedFeatures.notes: Video status model: DRAFT -> UPLOADING -> PROCESSING -> READY (or FAILED, with error_reason). publicId is an 11-char nanoid (varchar(11) column). VideoProcessor extends WorkerHost from @nestjs/bullmq v12 and routes by job.name; it is registered ONLY in WorkerModule (not VideosModule) to keep FFmpeg work out of the API process (TD-04). FfmpegService wraps child_process.execFile with an explicit Promise (not util.promisify) for testability. Stream/download use @Redirect + @Public with a dynamic presigned URL (302).

implementedFeatures.name: task-startup-infra — Planning Artifacts (in progress, uncommitted)
implementedFeatures.summary: Research, technical decisions, consolidated context and a clean validation for a Docker startup/infra reliability fix of the Phase 03 stack. Three decisions are finalized; implementation of the actual code/compose changes has not begun.
implementedFeatures.notes: TD-01: add a one-shot minio-init container (image with mc) that creates the $S3_BUCKET bucket idempotently (mc mb --ignore-existing); API and worker depend on it via condition: service_completed_successfully. TD-02: worker WorkerModule registers TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Video, Channel, User]) so the Video relation graph resolves in the worker's DataSource. TD-03: COPY package manifests + RUN npm ci inside Dockerfile.dev and Dockerfile.worker, plus an anonymous volume (- /home/node/app/node_modules) in compose.yaml so the source bind mount does not shadow the image's node_modules. Also add S3/Redis blocks to .env.example (hosts by Compose service name: minio, redis). Validation is clean (0 issues).

implemented: POST /auth/register — register new user (creates user + channel, sends confirmation email)
GET /auth/confirm-email?token= — confirm email with verification token
POST /auth/login — login, returns JWT access token in cookie
POST /auth/refresh — refresh access token using refresh token cookie
POST /auth/logout — invalidate refresh token, clear cookies
GET /auth/me — get current authenticated user info
POST /videos — initiate video creation and multipart upload (SI-03.3)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/presign-part — presign URL for a multipart upload part (SI-03.4)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/complete — complete multipart upload & enqueue processing job (SI-03.6)
POST /videos/:publicId/upload/abort — abort multipart upload, mark FAILED (SI-03.4)
GET /videos/:publicId — public video metadata, status, channel info, thumbnail URL (SI-03.9)
GET /videos/:publicId/stream — 302 redirect to presigned GET URL for streaming (SI-03.8)
GET /videos/:publicId/download — 302 redirect to presigned GET URL with attachment header (SI-03.8)

conventionsAndPatterns: Docker Compose service names as hosts — never localhost/127.0.0.1 in config
`docker compose up` brings up infrastructure only; nestjs-api and nestjs-worker idle (tail -f /dev/null); the server, worker and migrations are manual steps (start:dev, start:worker, migration:run)
NestJS modules: one module per domain; TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Entity]) in each module; forRootAsync only at app/worker root (never in feature modules)
An entity is only discovered (even with autoLoadEntities: true) if some module registers it via forFeature — the root cause behind the worker entity-graph decision
NestJS services own only their domain's entities; cross-domain access via service injection, not direct repository access
Config: @nestjs/config with namespaced registerAs(name, () => ({...})) factories — one file per domain in src/config/
Env validation: Joi schema in src/config/env.validation.ts passed to ConfigModule.forRoot
DomainException (common/exceptions/domain.exception.ts) for business rule violations, caught by DomainExceptionFilter
All NestJS routes protected by JwtAuthGuard globally; use @Public() decorator to expose public routes (e.g. video info/stream/download)
BullMQ worker: VideoProcessor extends WorkerHost from @nestjs/bullmq and routes by job.name in a single process() method; registered only in WorkerModule
FFmpeg: thin child_process.execFile wrapper (FfmpegService) with an explicit Promise — no fluent-ffmpeg dependency
Test file suffixes: .spec.ts (unit), .integration-spec.ts (integration), .e2e-spec.ts (E2E) — Jest filters by regex; e2e runs in band
Next.js BFF pattern: client calls /api/* route handlers which forward to NestJS; client never calls NestJS directly
OpenAPI types: lib/api/types.gen.ts — regenerate after backend changes with openapi:export + openapi-typescript
MSW mocks: next-frontend/mocks/handlers/ — enabled via MSW_ENABLED=true env var (server-side MSW)
RHF + Zod for frontend forms; error mapping via lib/auth/error-mapping.ts
Git Flow: feature/* and bugfix/* branches from dev, merge to dev; dev -> main when stable; never commit directly to main
Definition of Done: relevant + full test suite passes + tsc --noEmit exits 0 + npm run lint passes
Phase workflow is mandatory (research -> plan-context -> plan-validate -> plan-resolve -> plan-build -> implement); implementing without the research/planning artifacts is automatic rejection
